title: Etale-to-proetale comparison of the canonical direct-image projection morphism
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite discrete commutative ring and $p:X\to Y$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes. Work on small representatives of the etale and pro-etale sites in a common universe with ordinary uncompleted constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Put $F_T=\nu_T^*$, $u=p_{\mathrm{et}}^*$, $v=p_{\mathrm{proet}}^*$, $R_e=Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}$ and $R_p=Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}$. Use the canonical pullback comparison $a:F_Xu\xrightarrow{\sim}vF_Y$ [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], the tensor comparisons $t_T:F_T(B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_TB\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}F_TC$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and the normalized direct-image mate $b_B:F_YR_eB\xrightarrow{\sim}R_pF_XB$ for $B\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate].

Let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $N\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, and assume $L=K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}uN$ also lies in $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Let $\pi_e$ and $\pi_p$ denote the canonical projection morphisms at $(K,N)$ and $(F_XK,F_YN)$, respectively: each is the adjoint transpose of the pullback tensor comparison followed by counit tensor identity [def-kun-projection-formula-map, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Set $h=(1\otimes a_N)\circ t_{X;K,uN}$. Then, as maps from $F_Y(R_eK\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)$ to $R_p(F_XK\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}vF_YN)$,
$$R_p(h)\circ b_L\circ F_Y(\pi_e)=\pi_p\circ(b_K\otimes1)\circ t_{Y;R_eK,N}.$$
The equality is natural in the displayed inputs. Properness, constructibility, finite Tor amplitude and invertibility of the projection morphisms are not assumed.

proof.text: Use the ringed-topos square whose upper row is $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$, lower row is $\nu_Y:Y_{\mathrm{proet}}\to Y_{\mathrm{et}}$, and vertical maps are $p_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{et}}$. The comparison geometric morphisms and their fixed-$A$ module actions are [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]; their commutation comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Equip each corner with its constant commutative ring $A$. The structural maps preserve constant sections, by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] and the fixed-coefficient constructions. Thus the commutation comparison is a ringed one: naturality for zero, one, addition, multiplication and scalar action identifies these operations along both paths. This is a square of the kind in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], with no cartesianness assertion. Its derived inverse-image comparison in the direction used for exchange is $\theta:vF_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}F_Xu=a^{-1}$, with precisely the specified constant-module identifications.

source.place: Comparison square immediately preceding Tag 09A6, lemma-morphism-comparison; fixed constant coefficient ring identifications

proof.text: Let $\operatorname{Ex}_B:F_YR_eB\to R_pF_XB$ be the exchange mate of $\theta$ in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], its transpose under $v\dashv R_p$ is $F_X(\varepsilon^e_B)\circ a_{R_eB}^{-1}$. For $B=K$ and $B=L$, this is exactly the defining transpose of $b_B$ in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection gives $\operatorname{Ex}_K=b_K$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_L=b_L$. The hypotheses for these two normalized comparisons are satisfied: $p$ is qcqs, $A$ is finite discrete commutative, and $K,L\in D^+$. No lower bound on $N$ or on $R_eK\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram, specialized to the etale/pro-etale comparison square; tensor identifications from Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to this ringed square with $E=K$ and $Q=N$. Its projection maps are the adjuncts of pullback tensor comparison followed by counit tensor identity, hence are exactly $\pi_e$ and $\pi_p$ by [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Its tensor comparisons on the horizontal edges are the specified $t_X,t_Y$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The target identification in that theorem first applies $t_{X;K,uN}$ and then $1\otimes\theta_N^{-1}=1\otimes a_N$, so its direct image is exactly $R_p(h)$. Substitute the two mate identifications from step 2 in the theorem's equality. Its first route becomes $R_p(h)\circ b_L\circ F_Y(\pi_e)$; its second route becomes $\pi_p\circ(b_K\otimes1)\circ t_{Y;R_eK,N}$. This is the required equality in the ordinary uncompleted derived category.

source.place: Tag 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram, specialized to the etale/pro-etale comparison square; tensor identifications from Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product

proof.text: The equality used in step 3 is natural in $E,Q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]. The replacements $\operatorname{Ex}_B=b_B$ are identities of the specified components, and $b_B$ is natural on $D^+$ by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Restricting the naturality squares to morphisms of pairs $(K,N)$ for which both $K$ and $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}uN$ lie in $D^+$ therefore gives the claimed naturality. None of the cited square-compatibility or projection-map statements requires properness, constructibility, finite Tor amplitude, or invertibility of either projection morphism.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q14-59d6f9c07 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and all four steps, every cited statement, Stacks 0E48 (sites-cohomology.tex l.13715), 09A6 and blueprint main-20261015 sk-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite proof (3). The delivery creates no new nodes and leaves the statement unchanged; the proof specializes lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence to the square f=p_et, f'=p_proet, g=nu_Y, g'=nu_X. Step 1: theta is vF_Y->F_Xu, which is a^{-1}; naturality of a on constant sections plus uniqueness of constant-section-preserving maps gives a commutative square of ringed topoi, so the elementary flag is fine. Step 2: the mate's transpose is F_X(eps)∘a^{-1}, exactly q_{u,K} of the canonical-mate node, so Ex=b at K and at L (both D^+, p qcqs). Step 3: the composition identification is theta^{-1}=a, so it gives R_p(h); the projection maps match the def-kun and ringed-projection-mate definitions. The 07A4 comparisons of lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal and the ringed node agree definitionally on K-flat models, which I judged not a C1 fault. Step 4: naturality restricts to the admissible pairs. Edge cases checked: p=id, N the tensor unit, X empty, Z/4 with unbounded N, non-cartesian squares. No duplicate in the DAG; no cycle (the item is absent from the closures of all five main cited nodes). Parent step 5 uses the item only at bounded ctf inputs. The worker wrote three tool_uses itself (strictly L's field under C8); I accept them as generic tools that keep the unit's transport route. No SGA. No fixes.
